summary: Axiom Payments - duplicate streaming replies and sudden throttling causing transaction failures
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10T02:05 and 2026-03-10T03:30 UTC Axiom Payments reported duplicated streaming responses and a surge of 5xx errors plus client-observed throttling that caused ~18% of payment API calls to fail or be delayed beyond customer SLOs.
Impact: Transaction creation requests experienced duplicate model outputs (duplicate intents leading to double-charges in downstream processing) and elevated latency/timeouts across the us-east region. Customer reported immediate business impact (failed settlements).
Environment: Production (us-east) serving via Hosted API for enterprise tenant using model redwood-ggml-13B pinned version v2026-02-25. Customer on enterprise plan with dedicated routing policy.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a stream-based chat request with small initial prompt and repeated 'confirm' function call; 2) Observe two or more streamed final responses within 1s window for same request id; 3) Repeat under sustained concurrent load (~120 rps) and observe API gateway returning 429s or 502s.
Observed behavior: Streaming connection returned duplicate final chunks for ~12% of streams; API gateway returned 429s with message 'rate-limited' while backend showed no corresponding throttling in dedicated pool metrics.
Initial notes: Customer escalated to CS at 02:20 UTC. Triage opened and declared Sev1 due to financial impact. Temporary mitigation requested and SLA credit asked for.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Customer): We saw duplicate confirmations and some failed settlements. This is critical for today’s batch. Please advise workaround ASAP.
2026-03-10 - Carlos Ruiz (Support): Acknowledged. Eng oncall paged. Can you provide sample request IDs?
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Customer): Provided request ids: req_8f3a2b, req_8f3a2c, req_8f3a2d and a slack thread #support-axiom with screenshots.

2026-03-10 - Priya Nair (Oncall SRE): Investigating. Initial traces show multiple ACKs for the same stream ID; duplications originate at api-gateway -> stream-multiplexer handoff. Metrics: stream_ack_rate spiked ~2x at 02:04 UTC.
2026-03-10 - David Lee (Serving): Rolling back recent routing rule changes in us-east. Noted a recent config push 2026-03-10T01:58 by infra/terraform PR 1045.
2026-03-10 - Carlos Ruiz (Support): Customer notified of temporary rollback and traffic reroute to us-west cluster. They confirm partial recovery at 03:10 UTC.
2026-03-11 - Customer Success (Elena Park): Follow-up scheduled for postmortem and SLA credit discussion. Customer requested detailed root cause and timeline.
2026-03-13 - Carlos Ruiz (Support): Final resolution recorded and postmortem link shared. Customer accepted remediation steps and SLA credit plan.
investigation_notes: Timeline and evidence: At 01:58 UTC an infra routing config (PR 1045) introduced a new streaming multiplexer path intended to reduce cold-starts. At 02:03 UTC stream_ack_rate doubled and stream session state reconciliation lagged. Traces (trace ids: 7a1b3c, 7a1b4d) show api-gateway re-sending stream init frames when backend did not immediately ACK due to a lock contention in the multiplexer: this resulted in duplicate final chunks being emitted when the delayed original ACK arrived. Concurrently, a defensive token-bucket rate limiter in api-gateway had a regression that treated these duplicate frames as new requests and incremented counters, causing the gateway to return 429s even though dedicated pool metrics were below thresholds. Key logs: /logs/stream-multiplexer/2026-03-10.log lines 1124-1168; apigw metrics spike at 02:04. Root cause: a combination of (1) a non-idempotent stream init handshake in the multiplexer introduced by config change, and (2) a rate-limiter edge-case that double-counted retries. Evidence: reproducible with provided request ids when replayed in a staging environment with the problematic multiplexer enabled.
resolution_notes: Immediate fixes applied: 1) Rolled back the multiplexer path (infra PR revert) at 02:45 UTC which stopped new duplicates; 2) Disabled the new token-bucket defensive code path causing double-counts at 03:00 UTC; 3) Temporarily routed Axiom Payments traffic to us-west cluster for the remainder of the window; 4) Increased dedicated pool headroom by +20% for Axiom until full fix is deployed. Permanent remediation: 1) Code fix PR #2387 removed the non-idempotent handshake and adds idempotency tokens for stream inits; 2) Rate limiter fix added de-duplication check for retry frames and a test harness; 3) Add a canary rollout guard for infra routing changes and telemetry alerts for stream_ack anomalies. Follow-ups and customer remediation: Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-15; agreed SLA credit of one week of enterprise plan; instrumentation dashboard created (link below) and alerts added.
